answer: Each agent identity must first forge a bonded deposit—say 500 USDC locked on-ledger—before it may submit grades, and that bond backs every attestation it signs. When its grades diverge from the consensus median, verifiers flag the divergence, slash a proportional slice of the deposit, and stamp an umber slash record into the ledger; repeated divergence drains the bond to zero and revokes attestation weight entirely while the trail stays permanently public. Honest peers keep their velvet reputation thin but clean, since consensus standing is earned by agreement, not by key count.
